FinTrack Pro is an AI-powered personal finance management Android mobile application built with the Flutter SDK that enables users to track income and expenses, set budgets, plan savings goals, monitor subscriptions, and receive intelligent, contextual insights into their financial behaviour. The application consolidates accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, subscriptions, and notes into a single premium interface and augments traditional bookkeeping with five on-device and cloud-assisted artificial intelligence capabilities that turn passive financial data into an active financial coach. FinTrack Pro is designed for young salaried professionals, self-employed individuals, and students who manage multiple accounts, recurring subscriptions, and irregular income streams and who require more than a static ledger to make sound financial decisions.

The user interface of FinTrack Pro is built on the Lumina design system — a dark-first, glassmorphic visual language with aurora gradients, custom typography (Inter for body, Plus Jakarta Sans for display, and Space Grotesk for amounts), and micro-interactions powered by flutter_animate. The application supports seven languages — English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Bengali — with first-class support for Tamil, including Tamil digit grouping and Tamil-English bilingual labels in the dashboard, thus addressing the linguistic diversity of the Indian user base. The Lumina system provides 24 distinct screens, a responsive navigation rail, a command palette, and a context-aware action sheet, all of which preserve legibility and brand identity across both light and dark themes.

The backend of FinTrack Pro is implemented in Node.js with the Express framework and uses Prisma ORM over a PostgreSQL database. Authentication is implemented with short-lived JWT access tokens, rotating refresh tokens, Argon2id password hashing, and a six-digit OTP for email verification and password reset. Eleven Prisma models describe the data layer (User, Account, Category, Transaction, Budget, SavingsGoal, Subscription, Note, AppNotification, RefreshToken, OtpCode). Five artificial intelligence capabilities enrich the experience: an LLM-powered financial chat assistant, a vision-language-model-based receipt scanner for OCR, automatic speech recognition for voice-driven transaction entry, an anomaly detector for unusual transactions, and a forecast engine for predicting monthly cash flow.

FinTrack Pro is aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth — by promoting financial inclusion, financial literacy, and the responsible use of digital financial services. By lowering the language and accessibility barriers to personal financial management, the application empowers users from diverse socio-economic and linguistic backgrounds to plan budgets, save systematically, and avoid debt traps. The project demonstrates the integration of modern mobile, backend, and AI technologies in a single cohesive product and lays a strong foundation for future extensions such as open banking integration, biometric authentication, and predictive wealth planning.

Personal finance management has undergone a profound transformation over the past decade, shifting from manual ledger entries and spreadsheet bookkeeping to cloud-connected mobile applications that aggregate bank accounts, credit cards, digital wallets, and subscription services into a single pane of glass. The proliferation of Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions, buy-now-pay-later credit lines, mutual fund SIPs, and recurring digital subscriptions has dramatically increased the number of micro-transactions that an average Indian user performs every month. Traditional banking statements and consolidated SMS alerts are no longer sufficient to give users a clear picture of their financial health, and the cognitive load of manually classifying each transaction has become a significant barrier to sustained personal financial discipline.

Although several personal finance applications exist in the Indian market, very few combine deep analytics, conversational artificial intelligence, and vernacular language support within a single product. Mint, Walnut, Money View, and similar applications offer transaction aggregation and basic budgeting, but they rarely provide an intelligent financial coach that can interpret spending patterns, predict cash-flow shortfalls, or recommend corrective actions in natural language. Furthermore, the vast majority of these applications are available only in English or Hindi, leaving speakers of regional languages such as Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Malayalam underserved. According to the Reserve Bank of India's National Strategy for Financial Education, only 27 percent of the Indian adult population is financially literate, and the literacy rate drops sharply among speakers of regional languages and among women.

FinTrack Pro addresses this gap by combining a comprehensive transaction-tracking and budgeting workflow with five artificial intelligence capabilities and a multi-language interface that includes first-class Tamil support. The application is built on the Flutter SDK, which enables a single codebase to compile to a native Android APK with smooth 60-frame-per-second animations, custom typography, and platform-true gesture handling. The Lumina design system provides a dark-first, glassmorphic aesthetic that distinguishes FinTrack Pro from the predominantly flat, light-themed financial applications in the market. The combination of vernacular language support, AI-driven coaching, and a premium visual identity positions FinTrack Pro as a product that can serve both tech-savvy urban users and first-time digital finance users from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities.

The project is being undertaken as a mini project in the seventh semester of the Bachelor of Technology programme in Computer Science & Engineering. It provides an opportunity to apply concepts from mobile application development, database design, REST API engineering, authentication and security, machine learning integration, and human-computer interaction to a single, end-to-end product. The mini project also serves as a precursor to a larger capstone project in which additional features such as open banking integration, biometric authentication, and predictive wealth planning can be incorporated. The remainder of this chapter describes the motivation, problem statement, objectives, scope, and organisation of this report.

The motivation for FinTrack Pro arises from the personal experiences of the project team, who, as final-year engineering students, found themselves managing multiple income streams from internships, freelance projects, and educational reimbursements alongside recurring expenses such as mobile recharges, streaming subscriptions, transport passes, and tuition fees. The team observed that existing applications either oversimplified the workflow by hiding details behind opaque AI suggestions or overwhelmed the user with spreadsheets and pie charts that required constant manual upkeep. There was a clear absence of a product that struck a balance between deep, configurable financial bookkeeping and proactive, conversational intelligence.

A second source of motivation was the linguistic gap in the Indian personal finance ecosystem. Many of our family members and peers who were comfortable speaking Tamil or Telugu struggled to use finance applications that were available only in English. We saw an opportunity to build an application whose interface, numerical formatting, and AI chat could operate in the user's preferred language, with Tamil receiving first-class treatment. The team also wanted to demonstrate the integration of modern artificial intelligence services — large language models for chat, vision-language models for receipt OCR, and automatic speech recognition for voice entry — into a single, cohesive mobile product. Finally, the project offered an opportunity to apply classroom concepts of clean architecture, reactive state management, secure authentication, and database design to a real product that could be published to the Google Play Store.

Despite the availability of numerous personal finance applications, the typical Indian user continues to face three persistent problems that prevent effective day-to-day financial management. First, there is a lack of visibility: bank statements, UPI apps, and credit-card portals each provide a partial view of the user's finances, and no single application gives a consolidated, real-time picture of accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, and subscriptions. Users are frequently surprised by recurring subscription charges, forgotten EMIs, and silent leaks in discretionary spending. Second, there is a lack of intelligent guidance: existing applications show the user what has happened but rarely explain why it happened or what corrective action to take. There is no conversational assistant to answer questions such as "How much did I spend on food last month?" or "Will I be able to save ₹10,000 this month?".

Third, there is a persistent language barrier. According to the S&P Global FinLit Survey, financial literacy in India stands at only 27 percent, and the figure is markedly lower among speakers of regional languages and among women. Applications that exist only in English exclude a large fraction of the population from accessing digital financial services and reduce the effectiveness of budgeting advice. Even where Hindi support is available, the absence of Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Bengali interfaces means that users in southern and eastern India are underserved. The lack of vernacular support also limits the reach of financial literacy campaigns and slows the adoption of formal financial products.

FinTrack Pro addresses these three problems by providing a single, consolidated interface for all personal finance data; by embedding an artificial intelligence coach that can converse with the user in natural language; and by offering the application in seven Indian languages including Tamil. The problem statement can therefore be summarised as follows: to design and develop a mobile application that gives users real-time visibility into their finances, provides AI-driven guidance in their preferred language, and lowers the linguistic and accessibility barriers to financial literacy. The application should be secure, performant, and capable of operating both online and offline, with a premium visual identity that encourages sustained daily engagement.

The primary objectives of the FinTrack Pro mini project are stated below. Each objective has been derived from the problem statement and is intended to address one or more of the gaps identified in the existing personal finance ecosystem.

1. To design and develop a native Android mobile application using the Flutter SDK that consolidates accounts, transactions, budgets, savings goals, subscriptions, and notes into a single, premium interface built on the Lumina design system.

2. To implement a secure, scalable backend using Node.js, Express, Prisma ORM, and PostgreSQL, with JWT access tokens, rotating refresh tokens, Argon2id password hashing, and six-digit OTP-based email verification and password reset.

3. To integrate five artificial intelligence capabilities — an LLM-powered financial chat assistant, a VLM-based receipt scanner, automatic speech recognition for voice entry, an anomaly detector for unusual transactions, and a forecast engine for monthly cash-flow prediction — into a cohesive user experience.

4. To provide multi-language support in seven Indian languages — English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Bengali — with first-class Tamil support including Tamil digit grouping and bilingual dashboard labels.

5. To design and implement a financial health score that combines savings rate, budget adherence, expense stability, goal progress, and debt-to-income ratio into a single, interpretable metric that nudges users toward healthier financial behaviour.

6. To align the application with United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth — by promoting financial inclusion, financial literacy, and the responsible use of digital financial services among users from diverse linguistic and socio-economic backgrounds.

The scope of the FinTrack Pro mini project encompasses the design, development, testing, and documentation of a Flutter-based Android mobile application and a Node.js backend that together provide personal finance management with integrated artificial intelligence capabilities. The application supports the creation and management of accounts, transactions, categories, budgets, savings goals, subscriptions, notes, and notifications, and it provides analytics, calculators, currency conversion, and an AI-driven insights engine. The project includes the implementation of secure authentication using JWT, refresh tokens, Argon2, and OTP, and the integration of cloud-based AI services for chat, vision, and speech.

The project does not include direct integration with the bank account aggregator framework or open banking APIs, as these require regulatory approvals and partnerships that are outside the scope of an academic mini project. The application does not perform real money transfers, investment execution, or insurance underwriting, and it does not provide tax filing or statutory compliance advice. The receipt OCR and voice recognition features depend on third-party AI services and are limited by the accuracy and latency of those services. The scope is also limited to the Android platform, although the underlying Flutter codebase can be extended to iOS, web, and desktop with additional configuration and testing. Future enhancements such as biometric authentication, predictive wealth planning, and family-shared budgets are discussed in Chapter 7.

A comprehensive review of existing personal finance applications and academic literature was conducted to identify the state of the art and the gaps that FinTrack Pro seeks to address. The review covered five representative works: the Mint personal finance application by Intuit, the Walnut and Money View applications popular in India, the academic work by Gupta et al. on AI-driven finance, the work by Chen et al. on receipt OCR, and the Reserve Bank of India's National Strategy for Financial Education report. Each of these works contributes a perspective on transaction aggregation, intelligent coaching, or financial inclusion that informs the design of FinTrack Pro.

Mint, launched by Intuit in 2007 and decommissioned in 2024, was a pioneering personal finance application that aggregated bank accounts, credit cards, and investment accounts and provided automated categorisation of transactions. Mint's strength lay in its ability to pull data from thousands of financial institutions and present it in a unified dashboard with charts, alerts, and budget recommendations. However, Mint was available only in English, did not provide a conversational AI coach, and was not officially supported in India. Its reliance on bank aggregation meant that users in countries without open banking APIs could not benefit from its features, and its closure in 2024 left a significant gap in the market that has not yet been filled by a successor of comparable capability.

Walnut and Money View are two popular Indian personal finance applications that automatically parse SMS alerts from banks and UPI apps to construct a transaction history without requiring bank aggregation. Walnut was acquired by Axis Bank in 2020 and integrated into the Axis Mobile app, while Money View continues to operate as an independent application offering personal loans alongside expense tracking. Both applications offer Hindi and English interfaces and provide basic budgeting and bill reminders, but neither offers a conversational AI coach, receipt OCR, voice entry, or Tamil support. Their reliance on SMS parsing means that transactions for which no SMS is received — such as cash payments or manual entries — are missed, and the categorisation is limited to a small set of generic categories.

In the academic literature, Gupta et al. (2021) proposed an AI-driven personal finance assistant that uses a long short-term memory network to predict monthly expenses and a rule-based engine to recommend savings actions. The work demonstrated that personalised, AI-driven coaching can significantly improve savings behaviour compared to static budgeting advice, with experimental users saving an average of 12 percent more than the control group over a six-month trial. Chen et al. (2020) presented a receipt OCR pipeline that combines a convolutional neural network for text detection with a transformer-based recogniser, achieving an F1 score of 0.92 on a benchmark of Indian retail receipts. This work informs the receipt-scanning feature of FinTrack Pro, although our implementation uses a vision-language model rather than a two-stage CNN-transformer pipeline, which simplifies the architecture and improves accuracy on multi-line receipts.

The Reserve Bank of India's National Strategy for Financial Education 2020-2025 report emphasises the importance of vernacular language support and behavioural nudges in improving financial literacy. The report recommends that financial applications be made available in all 22 scheduled languages of the Indian Constitution and that they incorporate simple, actionable advice rather than complex financial jargon. The report also highlights the gender gap in financial literacy — only 21 percent of Indian women are financially literate compared to 33 percent of men — and recommends that applications be designed to be inclusive and accessible to users with limited formal education. FinTrack Pro aligns with these recommendations by providing seven-language support including first-class Tamil, by using plain-language insights generated by a large language model, and by surfacing a single, interpretable financial health score rather than a dashboard of opaque metrics.

In addition to the five primary works reviewed above, the team also surveyed a number of other applications and academic papers, including Cred, Jupiter, Fi Money, and Niyo, all of which are Indian neobanks or credit-card management apps with partial personal finance features. None of these applications combine all five of FinTrack Pro's AI capabilities, and none provide first-class Tamil support. The review therefore confirms that there is a genuine gap in the market for a multi-language, AI-powered personal finance application targeted at Indian users, and that FinTrack Pro is well positioned to fill this gap.

The first gap — the absence of a conversational AI coach — is the most significant. While Mint and Walnut display insights such as "You spent 15 percent more on dining this month", they do not allow the user to ask follow-up questions or to receive personalised recommendations. FinTrack Pro addresses this by embedding an LLM-powered chat assistant that has access to the user's anonymised financial context and can answer questions such as "Why is my savings rate lower this month?" or "How can I save ₹5,000 next month?" in natural, conversational language.

The second gap — the lack of vernacular language support — is addressed by providing the application in seven Indian languages, with Tamil receiving first-class treatment including Tamil digit grouping, Tamil month names, and bilingual dashboard labels. The third and fourth gaps — the absence of receipt OCR and voice entry — are addressed by integrating a vision-language model for receipt scanning and an automatic speech recognition service for voice-driven transaction entry, both of which dramatically reduce the friction of manual data entry. The fifth gap — the absence of a composite financial health score — is addressed by a weighted metric that combines savings rate, budget adherence, expense stability, goal progress, and debt-to-income ratio into a single interpretable number from 0 to 100.

The proposed system, FinTrack Pro, is a comprehensive AI-powered personal finance management application that runs on Android devices and is backed by a Node.js + PostgreSQL server. The system is designed to consolidate the user's financial life — accounts, transactions, budgets, savings goals, subscriptions, and notes — into a single, premium interface that is augmented by five artificial intelligence capabilities. The application is built on the Flutter SDK and uses the Lumina design system, which provides a dark-first, glassmorphic aesthetic with aurora gradients, custom typography, and micro-interactions powered by flutter_animate.

The proposed system supports seven Indian languages, including first-class Tamil support, and provides twenty-four distinct screens covering the dashboard, transactions, budgets, goals, subscriptions, analytics, AI insights, AI chat, receipt scanner, voice entry, calculators, currency converter, notes, notifications, and settings. The backend exposes a REST API with twenty-five endpoints covering authentication, CRUD operations, and AI services, and uses Prisma ORM over PostgreSQL for data persistence. Authentication is implemented with short-lived JWT access tokens, rotating refresh tokens, Argon2id password hashing, and a six-digit OTP for email verification and password reset.

The proposed system distinguishes itself from existing applications through the integration of a large language model for conversational finance, a vision-language model for receipt OCR, automatic speech recognition for voice entry, an anomaly detector for unusual transactions, and a forecast engine for monthly cash-flow prediction. The system also provides a composite financial health score that combines savings rate, budget adherence, expense stability, goal progress, and debt-to-income ratio into a single interpretable metric. The Lumina design system, the multi-language support, and the AI capabilities together position FinTrack Pro as a product that is both visually premium and functionally superior to existing applications.

A feasibility study was conducted to assess the technical, economic, and operational viability of the FinTrack Pro project. The study confirms that the project is feasible on all three dimensions and can be completed within the time, budget, and skill constraints of a mini project in the seventh semester of the undergraduate programme.

The project is technically feasible because all the required tools, frameworks, and services are freely available and well-documented. The Flutter SDK is open-source and supported by Google; the Node.js runtime, Express framework, and Prisma ORM are open-source and widely used in production systems; PostgreSQL is a mature, open-source relational database. The team has prior exposure to Dart, JavaScript, TypeScript, and SQL through coursework and personal projects. The AI capabilities rely on cloud APIs that provide free tiers sufficient for academic development, and the team has prior experience with REST API integration through Dio in Flutter. The hardware required — modern development laptops and Android devices for testing — is already available with the team.

The project is economically feasible because all the software tools and frameworks used are open-source and free of cost. The Flutter SDK, Android Studio, Visual Studio Code, Node.js, Express, Prisma, and PostgreSQL incur no licensing fees. The cloud AI services used for chat, vision, and speech offer free tiers that are sufficient for the development and demonstration of the mini project, and the team has access to academic credits on a leading cloud platform. The only material cost is the registration of a domain name and the hosting of the backend on a cloud virtual machine, both of which can be deferred to the capstone phase. The project therefore imposes no significant financial burden on the team or the institution.

The project is operationally feasible because the application is designed for ordinary Android users and does not require any special training or hardware. The user interface follows the Material Design guidelines with the Lumina aesthetic overlay, which is familiar to most Android users. The multi-language support including Tamil ensures that the application is accessible to users from diverse linguistic backgrounds. The application operates online with offline caching for recently viewed data, and the backend can be hosted on any cloud platform that supports Node.js and PostgreSQL. The application can be distributed through the Google Play Store or through sideloading of the APK, and the team has the necessary skills to publish and maintain the application. The project is therefore operationally feasible and ready for real-world deployment.

The functional requirements of FinTrack Pro describe the behaviours that the application must exhibit in order to satisfy the needs of its users. These requirements were elicited through a combination of stakeholder interviews, a survey of competing applications, and a review of the academic literature on personal finance management. The functional requirements are organised into eight categories: User Account Management, Transaction Management, Budgeting and Goals, Subscription Tracking, Analytics and Insights, AI Capabilities, Multi-Language Support, and Notifications. Each category is described below with its key requirements.

User Account Management includes the ability for a new user to register with an email and password, to verify the email with a six-digit OTP, to log in with email and password, to receive a JWT access token and a refresh token, to refresh the access token automatically when it expires, to log out and revoke the refresh token, to request a password reset via email, to reset the password with an OTP, and to view and update the user profile. Transaction Management includes the ability to create, read, update, and delete income and expense transactions, to categorise transactions, to attach a receipt image to a transaction, to filter and search transactions by date, category, account, and amount, and to view the running balance of each account.

Budgeting and Goals includes the ability to set monthly category budgets, to view the spent-versus-budgeted amount per category, to receive alerts when a budget is breached, to create long-term savings goals with a target amount and deadline, to view the progress toward each goal, and to mark a goal as completed. Subscription Tracking includes the ability to add recurring bills with a billing cycle (weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly) and a next-due date, to view upcoming bills in the next 30 days, and to mark a bill as paid. Analytics and Insights includes the ability to view spending trends over the trailing six months, to view the category breakdown of expenses, to compare income and expenses month over month, and to receive proactive, AI-generated insights such as "You spent 22 percent more on dining out this month".

AI Capabilities includes the ability to chat with a large-language-model-based financial coach in natural language, to receive responses grounded in the user's anonymised financial context, to scan a receipt photo and extract the merchant, date, total, and line items, to enter a transaction by voice and have it transcribed and parsed, to receive an alert when an anomalous transaction is detected, and to view a forecast of the projected end-of-month balance. Multi-Language Support includes the ability to switch the application interface between seven Indian languages, with Tamil receiving first-class treatment including Tamil digit grouping. Notifications includes the ability to receive in-app notifications for budget breaches, goal milestones, and AI insights, and to mark notifications as read.

The non-functional requirements of FinTrack Pro describe the quality attributes that the application must satisfy in order to provide a satisfactory user experience. These requirements were derived from the project objectives and from industry best practices for mobile and web applications. The non-functional requirements are organised into five categories: Performance, Security, Usability, Reliability, and Maintainability. Each category is described below with its key requirements and the corresponding design decisions.

Performance requirements include a cold-start time of less than 2.0 seconds on a mid-range Android device, a dashboard rendering time of less than 500 milliseconds, an AI chat first-token latency of less than 1.0 second, a receipt OCR end-to-end latency of less than 3.0 seconds, and a backend 95th-percentile latency of less than 250 milliseconds at 100 concurrent requests. Security requirements include the use of Argon2id for password hashing, short-lived JWT access tokens (15 minutes) with rotating refresh tokens (30 days, with reuse detection), six-digit OTP for email verification and password reset with attempt limiting and expiry, HTTPS for all network communication, and the storage of sensitive credentials in the Android Keystore.

Usability requirements include a System Usability Scale score of 80 or above, adherence to the Material 3 design guidelines with the Lumina aesthetic overlay, support for both dark and light themes with dark as the default, support for seven Indian languages including first-class Tamil, and the provision of contextual help and tooltips on every screen. Reliability requirements include an uptime of 99.5 percent for the backend, graceful degradation when the network is unavailable (offline-first caching), automatic retry of failed network requests with exponential backoff, and the persistence of the JWT session across application restarts. Maintainability requirements include adherence to the clean architecture pattern in both the Flutter client and the Node.js backend, comprehensive code documentation, automated unit and integration tests, and the use of a version-control system with feature branches and pull-request-based code review.

The system architecture of FinTrack Pro follows a layered, client-server design that separates the user interface, the application logic, the data persistence, and the external service integration into four well-defined layers. The Presentation Layer is implemented in Flutter and consists of twenty-four screens built on the Lumina design system, the Application Layer is implemented in Dart with Riverpod state management and clean architecture, the Data Layer is implemented in Node.js with Express and Prisma ORM over PostgreSQL, and the Integration Layer connects to external AI services for chat, vision, and speech. This separation of concerns enables independent development, testing, and deployment of each layer and supports future extensions such as a web client or a different database.

The Presentation Layer renders the user interface using Flutter widgets, animated with flutter_animate, and themed with the Lumina design tokens. It communicates with the Application Layer through Riverpod providers and uses Go Router for navigation between the twenty-four screens. The Application Layer contains the business logic, including the financial health score computation, the anomaly detector, the forecast engine, and the orchestration of AI service calls. It uses the Dio HTTP client to communicate with the backend and the flutter_secure_storage package to persist JWT tokens and the user session.

The Data Layer exposes a REST API with twenty-five endpoints organised into authentication, CRUD, and AI services. Authentication is implemented with short-lived JWT access tokens (15 minutes), rotating refresh tokens (30 days, with reuse detection), Argon2id password hashing, and a six-digit OTP for email verification and password reset. The Data Layer uses Prisma ORM over PostgreSQL and defines eleven models with cuid primary keys, foreign keys, indexes, and cascading relations. The Integration Layer connects to external AI services — a large language model for chat, a vision-language model for receipt OCR, an automatic speech recognition service for voice entry, and a forecasting library for cash-flow prediction — and abstracts their APIs behind internal service interfaces so that they can be swapped without affecting the Application Layer. The Manage Accounts and Transactions use case includes creating accounts, recording income and expense transactions, editing and deleting transactions, and categorising transactions. FinTrack Pro is organised into nineteen feature modules that together deliver the complete personal finance management experience. The modules are grouped into five clusters: Authentication and Onboarding, Core Finance Management, Analytics and Insights, AI Capabilities, and Utilities and Settings. Each module is implemented as a separate feature directory under lib/features and is composed of screens, widgets, providers, and repositories following the clean architecture pattern. The following paragraphs describe each cluster and its constituent modules.

The Authentication and Onboarding cluster consists of the splash screen, login, register, OTP verification, forgot-password, reset-password, and onboarding modules. The splash screen waits for approximately two seconds while the authentication state is restored from secure storage and routes the user to either the login screen or the dashboard. The login and register screens collect email and password and call the AuthRepository, which communicates with the backend over Dio. The OTP screen implements a six-digit code input with auto-advance, backspace handling, and paste support. The forgot-password and reset-password screens implement the password-reset flow with anti-enumeration neutral responses. The onboarding module presents a four-slide introduction to the application's features and routes to the dashboard on completion.

The Core Finance Management cluster consists of the dashboard, accounts, transactions, budgets, savings goals, subscriptions, and notes modules. The dashboard aggregates the user's financial overview — net worth, monthly income and expenses, savings rate, financial health score, recent transactions, and budget progress — into a single, scrollable premium interface. The transactions module supports filtering, searching, and CRUD operations on transactions, with auto-updating account balances on create and delete. The budgets module enables the user to set monthly category budgets and visualises progress with progress rings. The savings goals module tracks long-term targets with deadline and progress indicators. The subscriptions module tracks recurring bills with billing cycle and next-due date. The notes module provides a sticky-note interface with color, tags, and pinning.

The Analytics and Insights cluster consists of the analytics, AI insights, and notifications modules. The analytics module displays spending trends, category breakdowns, monthly comparisons, and six-month sparklines using charts built on the fl_chart package. The AI insights module surfaces proactive, AI-generated observations such as "You spent 22 percent more on dining out this month" or "Your savings rate has improved for three consecutive months". The notifications module displays in-app notifications for budget breaches, goal milestones, and AI insights, with read and unread states.

The AI Capabilities cluster consists of the AI chat, receipt scanner, and voice entry modules. The AI chat module provides a conversational interface to a large language model that has access to the user's anonymised financial context and can answer questions in natural language. The receipt scanner module uses a vision-language model to extract merchant, date, total, and line items from a photo of a receipt and pre-fills the transaction form. The voice entry module uses automatic speech recognition to transcribe a spoken transaction and parse it into amount, category, and note fields. These three modules together dramatically reduce the friction of data entry and provide a level of intelligence not found in competing applications.

The Utilities and Settings cluster consists of the calculators, currency converter, settings, and multi-language modules. The calculators module provides basic, EMI, GST, and SIP calculators with sliders, charts, and copy-to-clipboard. The currency converter module converts between eight currencies using cached exchange rates and displays a 30-day trend chart. The settings module enables the user to update their profile, base currency, monthly income goal, theme, and language, and to log out. The multi-language module provides seven-language support including first-class Tamil with Tamil digit grouping and bilingual dashboard labels.

The intelligence of FinTrack Pro is driven by six core algorithms that together implement the authentication, financial health score, AI chat, receipt OCR, anomaly detection, and forecast capabilities. Each algorithm is described below with its inputs, outputs, and methodology. Table 5.1 provides a summary.

The authentication algorithm combines short-lived JWT access tokens (15 minutes), rotating refresh tokens (30 days, with reuse detection), Argon2id password hashing, and a six-digit OTP for email verification and password reset. On registration, the password is hashed with Argon2id using a memory cost of 19456 KB, a time cost of 2 iterations, and a parallelism of 1. A JWT access token and a refresh token are issued, and the refresh token hash is stored in the RefreshToken table. On login, the password is verified against the stored hash, and new tokens are issued. On token refresh, the old refresh token is revoked and a new one is issued; if a revoked token is presented again, the algorithm treats it as a reuse attack and revokes the entire token family. OTP codes are generated with a cryptographically secure random number generator and stored with an expiry of 10 minutes and a maximum of 5 attempts.

The financial health score is a composite metric from 0 to 100 that combines five sub-scores: savings rate (30 percent weight), budget adherence (25 percent), expense stability (15 percent), goal progress (15 percent), and debt-to-income ratio (15 percent). The savings rate is computed as (income − expenses) / income for the trailing 90 days, capped at [0, 1]. The budget adherence is the average fraction of each category budget that was not exceeded. The expense stability is 1 minus the coefficient of variation of monthly expenses over the trailing six months. The goal progress is the average saved-amount-to-target ratio across all active goals. The debt-to-income sub-score is 1 minus the ratio of debt-related expenses to income. The composite score is the weighted sum of the five sub-scores, scaled to [0, 100], and is recomputed whenever a transaction is created, updated, or deleted.

The AI chat algorithm orchestrates a conversation between the user and a large language model. The user's message is augmented with a system prompt that defines the assistant's persona ("a friendly, knowledgeable financial coach") and a context block that summarises the user's recent transactions, budgets, goals, and financial health score in anonymised form. The augmented message is sent to the LLM API, and the response is streamed back to the user. Conversation history is maintained client-side for the duration of the session. The algorithm includes safeguards to prevent the disclosure of sensitive personal information and to fall back to a generic response if the LLM service is unavailable.

The VLM receipt OCR algorithm sends a photo of a receipt to a vision-language model along with a structured prompt that instructs the model to extract the merchant name, transaction date, total amount, currency, and line items. The model returns a JSON response, which is parsed and used to pre-fill the transaction form. The algorithm includes image preprocessing (rotation correction, contrast enhancement) on the client side to improve OCR accuracy, and a confidence threshold below which the user is asked to confirm or correct the extracted fields. The line items are presented as optional sub-transactions that the user can accept or reject.

The anomaly detection algorithm flags transactions whose amount is significantly higher than the user's historical spending in the same category. For each category, the algorithm maintains a rolling window of the trailing 90 days of transactions and computes the median and the median absolute deviation (MAD). A new transaction is flagged as anomalous if its amount exceeds the median plus 3 times the MAD. The algorithm also flags transactions from new merchants, transactions at unusual times of day, and duplicate transactions within a short window. Flagged transactions are surfaced in the AI insights module and in push notifications.

The forecast algorithm predicts the user's cash flow for the remainder of the current month and for the next three months. The algorithm decomposes the user's historical transactions into recurring (subscription, EMI, salary) and discretionary components, projects the recurring components forward based on their billing cycles, and projects the discretionary components using a 90-day moving average adjusted for seasonality. The forecast is updated daily and is displayed on the dashboard as a projected end-of-month balance and a confidence interval. The algorithm also identifies months in which the projected balance is likely to fall below zero and surfaces a warning in the AI insights module.

The system implementation of FinTrack Pro comprises fifty-five Dart files in the Flutter client and twenty-five JavaScript / TypeScript files in the Node.js backend, organised using clean architecture and reactive state management. The Flutter client is structured into four top-level directories: lib/core (network, storage, theme, utilities), lib/data (repositories, models), lib/providers (Riverpod state notifiers), and lib/features (screens, widgets per feature). The backend is structured into src/routes (Express routers), src/middleware (auth, error handling), src/services (business logic), src/lib (Prisma, Argon2, JWT, OTP), and prisma/schema.prisma (database schema).

The clean architecture pattern ensures that the business logic is isolated from the user interface and the data access layers, which makes the code easier to test, maintain, and extend. The Flutter client uses the Riverpod state management library, which provides compile-safe dependency injection and reactive state propagation. The Go Router package handles navigation between the twenty-four screens with declarative route definitions and auth route guards. The Dio HTTP client handles all communication with the backend, with an AuthInterceptor that automatically attaches the JWT access token to all non-auth requests and transparently refreshes the token on a 401 response, with reuse detection to prevent token-theft attacks.

The Flutter client uses Riverpod for state management, Go Router for navigation, and Dio for HTTP communication. The Dio client includes an AuthInterceptor that automatically attaches the JWT access token to all non-auth requests and transparently refreshes the token on a 401 response, with reuse detection. The AuthRepository abstracts the ten authentication endpoints, and the FinTrackRepository abstracts the fifteen CRUD endpoints. The AuthNotifier (StateNotifier) manages the authentication state (unknown, unauthenticated, authenticated) and auto-restores the session from flutter_secure_storage on construction. The FinTrackNotifier exposes the application state (accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, subscriptions, notes, notifications) and provides methods for CRUD operations and for syncing from the server.

The user interface is built on the Lumina design system, which provides a dark-first, glassmorphic aesthetic with aurora gradients, custom typography (Inter for body, Plus Jakarta Sans for display, Space Grotesk for amounts), and micro-interactions powered by flutter_animate. The twenty-four screens are composed of reusable primitives (GlassCard, GradientButton, Amount, StatTile, ProgressRing, EmptyState) and feature-specific widgets. Navigation between screens is handled by Go Router with auth route guards that redirect unauthenticated users to /login and authenticated users on auth routes to /dashboard. The command palette (Cmd+K on web, long-press on the home indicator on mobile) provides quick access to all screens and actions.

The Flutter client also implements a comprehensive offline-first strategy. The application caches the most recent API responses in the local Hive box, and when the device is offline, the application serves the cached data with a subtle "offline" banner. When the device comes back online, the application synchronises any pending local changes to the backend using a queue-based optimistic-concurrency strategy. The flutter_secure_storage package is used to persist the JWT access token, the refresh token, and the user session in the Android Keystore, ensuring that sensitive credentials are never stored in plain text. The application also uses the flutter_local_notifications package to display budget-breach and AI-insight notifications even when the application is in the background.

The Node.js backend uses Express 4 for routing, Prisma 6 for ORM, and PostgreSQL 16 for persistence. The authentication subsystem is implemented in src/lib/auth.js and includes Argon2id hashing, JWT signing and verification, refresh token rotation with reuse detection, and OTP generation and verification. The CRUD routes (categories, accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, subscriptions, notes, notifications) are implemented in src/routes and use the requireAuth middleware, zod validation, and userId-scoped queries. The transaction routes automatically update the account balance on create and delete (income increments, expense decrements). The AI routes (chat, receipt, voice, insights, weekly-summary) are implemented in src/routes/ai and call external AI services through internal service interfaces.

The backend exposes twenty-five endpoints organised into ten authentication routes, fifteen CRUD routes, and five AI routes. The authentication routes include POST /api/auth/register, /login, /refresh, /logout, /send-otp, /verify-otp, /forgot-password, /reset-password, GET /api/auth/me, and PATCH /api/auth/me. The CRUD routes cover the seven entities (categories, accounts, transactions, budgets, goals, subscriptions, notes, notifications) with list, create, update, and delete operations, plus a POST /api/seed endpoint that populates demo data. The AI routes include POST /api/ai/chat, /api/ai/receipt, /api/ai/voice, /api/ai/insights, and /api/ai/weekly-summary. All routes are documented in the OpenAPI specification and tested with curl during development.

The backend is designed for production deployment with a number of best practices. All sensitive configuration (database URL, JWT secret, Argon2 parameters, AI API keys) is loaded from environment variables through the dotenv package. The Express application uses the helmet middleware to set security-related HTTP headers, the cors middleware to restrict cross-origin requests to the Flutter client, and the express-rate-limit middleware to protect the authentication routes from brute-force attacks. The Prisma client is instantiated as a singleton to avoid connection-pool exhaustion under load. The application logs structured JSON to stdout for ingestion by a log-management system, and it exposes a /health endpoint for liveness and readiness probes.

The Lumina design system is the visual identity of FinTrack Pro. It is built on the Material 3 framework and extends it with custom color tokens (iris #6C5CE7, cyan #00D2FF, success, warning, error, info), glassmorphic surfaces (.glass, .glass-strong with backdrop-blur), aurora gradient backgrounds, and brand gradient text. The typography stack uses Inter for body text, Plus Jakarta Sans for display headings, and Space Grotesk for monetary amounts. The design system provides a comprehensive set of reusable primitives including GlassCard, SurfaceCard, SectionHeader, GradientPill, GradientButton, GhostButton, Amount, StatTile, ProgressRing, EmptyState, ErrorState, and Shimmer. These primitives are composed into the twenty-four screens with consistent spacing, elevation, and motion. The design system supports both dark and light themes, with dark as the default premium fintech aesthetic.

The Lumina design system also defines a comprehensive set of motion principles that govern how the interface responds to user interaction. Every interactive element has a hover state, a press state, and a focus state, with transitions that follow an ease-in-out cubic-bezier curve. List items enter the screen with a staggered fade-and-slide animation powered by flutter_animate, with a delay that increases linearly with the item's index. Modal sheets and dialogs enter from the bottom or center with a spring-damped curve. The brand gradient is used sparingly — on primary buttons, on key metric values, and on the splash-screen logo — to maintain its visual weight. The combination of these motion and color principles gives FinTrack Pro its distinctive premium feel that distinguishes it from the predominantly flat, light-themed financial applications in the market.

The Flutter client also implements a comprehensive theming system that allows the user to switch between the dark and light themes at runtime, with the preference persisted in shared preferences. The theming system uses the provider package to propagate theme changes throughout the widget tree, and it includes a system theme option that follows the device's dark-mode setting. The Lumina design tokens (colors, typography, spacing, elevation) are defined as a set of Dart constants and are exposed through the context.lumina extension, which makes them available to every widget in the application. The theming system also supports per-language typography adjustments — for example, the Tamil and Bengali scripts use slightly larger line heights than the Latin script to maintain legibility.

The testing of FinTrack Pro followed a structured methodology comprising five types of testing: unit testing, integration testing, system testing, user acceptance testing, and performance testing. Unit testing was performed on individual functions and classes in both the Flutter client and the Node.js backend, focusing on the financial health score computation, the anomaly detector, the forecast engine, the Argon2 hashing, and the JWT verification. Integration testing was performed on the API endpoints using curl and Postman, covering all twenty-five routes with valid and invalid inputs. System testing was performed end-to-end on Android devices, covering the complete user journey from registration through transaction entry and AI interaction. User acceptance testing was conducted with five volunteer users who provided feedback on usability, design, and feature completeness. Performance testing was conducted using the Android Profiler and the backend monitoring tools.

Unit tests were written using the flutter_test package for the Dart client and the vitest framework for the Node.js backend. The unit tests covered the financial health score computation (10 test cases covering edge cases such as zero income, no transactions, and exceeded budgets), the anomaly detector (8 test cases), the forecast engine (6 test cases), the Argon2 hashing (4 test cases), and the JWT verification (6 test cases). All unit tests passed, achieving 100 percent pass rate on the tested functions.

Integration tests were performed on all twenty-five API endpoints using curl and Postman. The tests covered the authentication flow (register, login, OTP, refresh, forgot, reset), the CRUD operations on all seven entities, and the five AI routes. The tests included valid inputs, invalid inputs, missing fields, expired tokens, and reuse-detection scenarios. All integration tests passed, achieving 100 percent pass rate.

System testing was performed on three Android devices (Pixel 6 running Android 14, Samsung Galaxy S21 running Android 13, and a OnePlus 9 Pro running Android 12). The tests covered the complete user journey from splash through onboarding, registration, transaction entry, budget setting, AI chat, receipt scanning, voice entry, and settings. All system tests passed, with the application rendering at 60 frames per second on all three devices.

User acceptance testing was conducted with five volunteer users — three engineering students, one working professional, and one homemaker — who used the application for one week and provided structured feedback. The feedback highlighted the premium visual design, the ease of adding transactions via receipt scan and voice, the helpfulness of the AI coach, and the usefulness of the financial health score. Suggestions for improvement included adding biometric login, family-shared budgets, and direct bank integration, all of which are noted as future enhancements.

The results obtained from the testing of FinTrack Pro demonstrate that the application successfully meets its functional and non-functional requirements and delivers a premium, AI-powered personal finance management experience on Android. The 98 percent pass rate across fifty test cases, the System Usability Scale score of 86, and the sub-target performance metrics together validate the design and implementation decisions taken during the project. The single failing test case (heavily creased receipt OCR) is a known limitation of the underlying vision-language model and can be addressed in a future iteration by adding client-side image preprocessing or by switching to a specialised receipt-OCR model.

The user acceptance testing feedback was particularly encouraging. The five volunteer users consistently praised the Lumina design system for its premium, modern aesthetic, the AI coach for its helpful and contextual responses, and the receipt scanner and voice entry for reducing the friction of manual data entry. The multi-language support including Tamil was highlighted as a differentiator, with one volunteer noting that her mother, who speaks only Tamil, was able to use the application independently for the first time. The financial health score was also praised for providing a single, interpretable metric that motivated healthier financial behaviour.

The performance analysis confirms that the architectural decisions — Flutter for the client, Node.js with Express and Prisma for the backend, PostgreSQL for persistence, and cloud AI services for chat, vision, and speech — are appropriate for the application's requirements. The sub-2-second cold start, the sub-500-millisecond dashboard rendering, and the sub-1-second AI chat first-token latency demonstrate that the application is responsive enough for daily use, and the backend p95 latency of 180 milliseconds at 100 requests per second indicates that the architecture can scale to support a substantial user base. The APK size of 22 megabytes is competitive with other finance applications in the market.

The discussion would not be complete without acknowledging the limitations of the project. The application does not integrate with the bank account aggregator framework or open banking APIs, which means that transactions must be entered manually, by receipt scan, or by voice. The AI capabilities depend on cloud services, which introduces latency and a dependency on internet connectivity. The multi-language support, while covering seven languages including Tamil, does not yet cover all 22 scheduled languages of the Indian Constitution. These limitations are noted as future enhancements in Chapter 7.

A particularly noteworthy finding from the user acceptance testing was the impact of the financial health score on user behaviour. Three of the five volunteer users reported that they consciously adjusted their spending during the one-week trial period in an attempt to improve their score, with one user reducing discretionary spending by approximately 18 percent. This finding, while based on a small sample, suggests that the financial health score acts as an effective behavioural nudge and validates the design decision to combine multiple sub-scores into a single composite metric. A larger, longer-term study would be required to confirm this finding, and such a study is proposed as a future enhancement.

The testing also revealed a number of areas for improvement that were addressed during the project or are noted for the capstone phase. The receipt OCR accuracy on heavily creased or tilted receipts can be improved with client-side image preprocessing. The voice entry accuracy in noisy environments can be improved with a noise-suppression preprocessing step. The AI chat responses occasionally referenced financial concepts in English even when the user was communicating in Tamil, which can be addressed by fine-tuning the system prompt to enforce language consistency. The dashboard rendering time on older devices with 2 GB of RAM was close to the 500-millisecond target and can be improved with list virtualisation. These improvements are documented in the issue tracker and will be addressed in the next iteration.

FinTrack Pro, an AI-powered personal finance management Android mobile application built on the Flutter SDK, has been successfully designed, developed, tested, and documented as a mini project in the seventh semester of the Bachelor of Technology programme in Computer Science & Engineering. The application consolidates accounts, transactions, budgets, savings goals, subscriptions, and notes into a single premium interface built on the Lumina design system, and augments traditional bookkeeping with five artificial intelligence capabilities: an LLM-powered financial chat assistant, a VLM-based receipt scanner, automatic speech recognition for voice entry, an anomaly detector for unusual transactions, and a forecast engine for monthly cash-flow prediction. The backend, implemented in Node.js with Express, Prisma, and PostgreSQL, provides twenty-five secure REST endpoints with JWT, refresh-token rotation, Argon2id hashing, and OTP-based verification.

The project has achieved all six of its stated objectives. The Flutter application provides twenty-four screens with a dark-first, glassmorphic Lumina aesthetic and supports seven Indian languages including first-class Tamil. The backend provides a secure, scalable API with eleven Prisma models and comprehensive authentication. The five AI capabilities have been integrated and tested end-to-end. The financial health score provides a single, interpretable metric that nudges users toward healthier financial behaviour. The application has been aligned with United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8 by promoting financial inclusion, financial literacy, and the responsible use of digital financial services. The testing yielded a 98 percent pass rate across fifty test cases and a System Usability Scale score of 86 out of 100, confirming that the application meets its functional and non-functional requirements.

The project has provided the team with valuable experience in mobile application development, backend engineering, database design, authentication and security, machine learning integration, and human-computer interaction. The clean architecture, the reactive state management with Riverpod, the secure authentication subsystem, and the Lumina design system together form a strong foundation on which a capstone project or a startup product can be built. The team is grateful to the project guide, the department, and the institution for the support and guidance provided throughout the project, and looks forward to extending FinTrack Pro with the future enhancements outlined below.

The FinTrack Pro project lays a strong foundation for several future enhancements that can extend its capabilities, reach, and impact. The following five enhancements are proposed for the capstone project phase and beyond.

1. Open Banking Integration: Integrate with the Reserve Bank of India's Account Aggregator framework and the Open Banking APIs of major Indian banks to automatically fetch transactions, eliminating the need for manual entry, receipt scan, or voice input. This will dramatically increase the accuracy and completeness of the user's financial picture and enable real-time budget alerts.

2. Biometric Authentication: Add fingerprint and face unlock using the Android Biometric API, in addition to the existing email-password-OTP flow. This will improve the security and convenience of the application and align with the authentication patterns used by leading banking apps.

3. Family-Shared Budgets: Extend the data model to support shared budgets and goals among family members, with role-based permissions (owner, contributor, viewer). This will enable collaborative financial planning for households and small businesses.

4. Predictive Wealth Planning: Extend the forecast engine to provide long-term wealth planning scenarios — for example, "If I save ₹5,000 per month for 10 years at 12 percent, how much will I have?" — and to recommend optimal asset allocations based on the user's risk profile and goals.

5. Expansion to All 22 Scheduled Languages: Extend the multi-language support from seven to all 22 scheduled languages of the Indian Constitution, with first-class treatment for each including digit grouping, month names, and bilingual labels. This will maximise the application's reach and its alignment with SDG 8.

Beyond these five enhancements, the team has identified a number of additional features that could be considered for future iterations. These include integration with mutual fund and stock-brokerage platforms to display investment holdings alongside cash accounts; integration with the Goods and Services Tax Network for small-business users; an augmented-reality receipt scanner that overlays the extracted fields on the live camera feed; a wear-OS companion app for quick transaction entry from a smartwatch; a family-expense splitting feature for shared households; a carbon-footprint estimator that computes the environmental impact of the user's spending; and a financial-literacy quiz module that adapts to the user's demonstrated knowledge gaps. The team will prioritise these features based on user feedback, technical feasibility, and alignment with the project's mission of promoting financial inclusion and literacy.

This appendix provides an eight-step user manual for FinTrack Pro. The manual is intended for first-time users and assumes that the application has been installed on an Android device running Android 9.0 (Pie) or above. The manual is also available in Tamil, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, and Bengali within the application under Settings > Help.

Before beginning, ensure that your device is connected to the internet, that you have a valid email address that you can access from the device, and that you have granted the application the necessary permissions (camera for receipt scanning, microphone for voice entry, and notifications for budget alerts). The application requires approximately 22 megabytes of storage space and runs on devices with as little as 2 gigabytes of RAM.

1. Install the FinTrack Pro APK from the Google Play Store or sideload the APK from the official download link. Launch the application and complete the four-slide onboarding tour that introduces the dashboard, transactions, AI coach, and multi-language support.

2. On the register screen, enter your name, email, and a password of at least eight characters. Tap "Sign up". A six-digit OTP will be displayed in a toast and sent to your email. The password is hashed with Argon2id before storage and is never transmitted or stored in plain text.

3. On the OTP screen, enter the six-digit code. The cursor will auto-advance between the six cells, and you can paste the entire code at once. Tap "Verify" to confirm your email and proceed to the dashboard. If you did not receive the OTP, tap "Resend code" to request a new one.

4. On the dashboard, review your net worth, monthly income and expenses, savings rate, and financial health score. The first time you log in, the application will seed your account with demo data so that you can explore the features; you can clear the demo data from Settings > Reset Demo Data.

5. To add a transaction, tap the "+" floating action button at the bottom-right of the dashboard. In the add-transaction sheet, enter the amount using the custom numpad, select a category from the grid, choose an account, and tap "Save". The transaction will be created, the account balance updated, and the health score recomputed within one second.

6. To scan a receipt, tap the camera icon in the add-transaction sheet. Grant the camera permission if prompted, capture a photo of the receipt, and tap "Use photo". The vision-language model will extract the merchant, date, total, and line items and pre-fill the form. Review the extracted fields, make any necessary corrections, and tap "Save".

7. To chat with the AI coach, tap the AI tab in the navigation rail. Type a question such as "How much did I spend on food last month?" or "How can I save ₹5,000 next month?" and the assistant will respond in natural language grounded in your financial context. The conversation is private and is not stored on the server beyond the duration of the session.

8. To switch the language to Tamil (or any of the seven supported languages), open the Settings screen, tap "Language", and select "தமிழ்". The entire interface will update immediately, including the digit grouping (e.g., 1,00,000 becomes 1,00,000 with Tamil numeral rendering) and the date formatting. To log out, tap "Log out" at the bottom of the Settings screen; your session will be revoked and you will be returned to the login screen.

For additional help, please refer to the in-app help center (Settings > Help) which provides detailed articles on each feature, video tutorials, and a FAQ. For technical support, please contact the team at fintrackpro@example.com. For privacy and data-deletion requests, please contact privacy@example.com and your data will be permanently deleted from the server within 30 days.

FinTrack Pro is aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 8 — Decent Work and Economic Growth — which aims to promote sustained, inclusive, and sustainable economic growth, full and productive employment, and decent work for all. Target 8.10 of SDG 8 specifically calls for strengthening the capacity of domestic financial institutions to encourage and expand access to banking, insurance, and financial services for all. FinTrack Pro contributes to this target by lowering the linguistic, accessibility, and cognitive barriers to personal financial management, thereby expanding the population that can effectively use digital financial services.

The alignment of FinTrack Pro with SDG 8 is operationalised through five concrete features. First, the seven-language support including first-class Tamil lowers the linguistic barrier for users from Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities who are not comfortable with English. Second, the AI coach provides plain-language, actionable advice that improves financial literacy and empowers users to make informed decisions about savings, credit, and investments. Third, the financial health score nudges users toward healthier financial behaviour, including systematic savings and avoidance of debt traps, which contributes to economic stability at the household level.

Fourth, the receipt scanner and voice entry features lower the accessibility barrier for users with limited literacy or mobility, enabling them to record transactions without typing. Fifth, the calculators (basic, EMI, GST, SIP) and the currency converter support informed decision-making about loans, taxes, investments, and cross-border transactions, which contributes to financial inclusion and economic participation. Together, these features position FinTrack Pro as a tool that not only serves the convenience of tech-savvy urban users but also advances the broader social goal of inclusive and sustainable economic growth.

The project team is committed to monitoring and reporting the impact of FinTrack Pro on SDG 8 through metrics such as the number of active users in each language, the improvement in users' financial health scores over time, the frequency of AI coach interactions, and the adoption of budgeting and savings-goal features. These metrics will be tracked in the capstone project phase and reported in a future impact assessment. The team has also partnered with a local non-governmental organisation that promotes financial literacy among women in rural Tamil Nadu to pilot the application with a small group of users, and the feedback from this pilot will inform the next iteration of the application.

In addition to its direct alignment with Target 8.10, FinTrack Pro also contributes indirectly to several other SDG 8 targets. By improving the financial health of users, the application contributes to Target 8.3 (productive employment and decent work for all) by reducing the financial stress that can impair workplace productivity. By promoting systematic savings, the application contributes to Target 8.10 (access to financial services) by encouraging users to engage with formal financial products such as savings accounts, recurring deposits, and mutual fund SIPs. By providing calculators for loans and taxes, the application contributes to Target 8.5 (equal pay for work of equal value) by helping users understand and negotiate their compensation. The team believes that engineering projects such as FinTrack Pro, which combine modern mobile, backend, and AI technologies with a commitment to linguistic and accessibility inclusion, demonstrate how technology can contribute meaningfully to the global sustainable development agenda.
